title: Slopes as simple machines
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 6 Science and Technology; not yet checked by a CBC Science and Technology teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: A plank against a pile of books, a toy car or a brick with a spring balance (or a rubber band to show the pull), a ramp at the school, a wedge (an axe head picture, a door stop) and a screw. The child compares the pull up two slopes before any rule is given.

skills.key_step: The child identifies slopes used as simple machines (ramps, inclined planes such as winding roads and staircases, wedges such as an axe or a knife, screws) by a sloping surface.

floor.question: Is a bottle opener a simple machine?

representations: a paper triangle wound round a pencil
pictures of an axe, a ramp and a winding road
steps: Ramp or inclined plane: a flat slope.
Wedge: two slopes back to back (axe, knife).
Screw: a slope wound round a rod.
contexts: a ramp into a lorry at a market

board.do: Draw a ramp, an axe head and a screw.

board.say: Where are the slopes on an axe?

board.do: Wait for "the two sides of the blade".

misconceptions.ask: Does a pulley have a sloping surface?
misconceptions.repair: Pulleys and see-saws are not slopes.

listen_for: a flat road is a slope
misconceptions.ask: Does a flat road go up?
misconceptions.repair: A slope rises from low to high.

listen_for: an axe is not a slope
misconceptions.ask: Look at the side of the blade: is it sloping?
What did the paper triangle make round the pencil?
misconceptions.repair: A screw thread is a wound slope.

checks.question: Is a knife blade a kind of slope?
Give one example of an inclined plane.
checks.answer: a ramp, a winding road or a staircase

skills.key_step: The child explains a slope makes it easier to raise a load: a gentler, longer slope needs less effort, but the load is moved a longer distance, so the work is not reduced.
representations: a brick pulled up a steep and a gentle plank with a rubber band
a drawing of two ramps to the same height
steps: Lift the brick straight up: big pull.
Pull it up a steep plank: less.
Pull it up a gentle, longer plank: least.
The distance pulled is longer each time.
contexts: pushing a wheelchair up a ramp
rolling a drum onto a lorry
a road zigzagging up a hill

board.do: Draw two ramps to the same height: one steep and short, one gentle and long.

misconceptions.ask: Which plank stretched the rubber band less?
misconceptions.repair: A gentler slope needs less effort.

misconceptions.ask: Did the brick change its weight?
misconceptions.repair: The load is the same; the effort is less.

misconceptions.ask: Which is longer: up the ramp or straight up?
misconceptions.repair: A slope is a longer way.

misconceptions.ask: Is the pull less but the distance more?
misconceptions.repair: Less effort over a longer distance.

checks.question: Which needs less effort to raise a load: a steep slope or a gentle one?
Why do roads up steep hills wind from side to side?
checks.answer: a longer, gentler slope needs less effort
